findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "email" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Validate an email address before using it: syntax, whether the domain exists and accepts mail (MX records), disposable or throwaway provider detection, role add…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: extract, summarize, screenshot, describe, email, papers · Private data: domain, token, wallet, transcribe, btc-address, email, base-allowance, ens · Public sink: domain, image, email · Destructive: summarize.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: extract, summarize, screenshot, describe, email, papers · Private data: domain, token, wallet, transcribe, btc-address, email, base-allowance, ens · Public sink: domain, image, email · Destructive: summarize

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
